# powerhmc_lpar (Resource)

Manages a Logical Partition (LPAR) on an IBM Power Systems managed system.

An LPAR is a virtual server carved out of a managed system's memory, processor,
and I/O resources. Use this resource to create AIX/Linux or IBM i partitions and
attach virtual networks, physical volumes, and virtual Fibre Channel adapters.

~> **LPARs are immutable.** Every managed attribute forces
destroy-and-recreate. Changing an attribute in place returns an
`Update Not Supported` error — Terraform will replace the partition instead.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The powerhmc_lpar resource creates and manages a Logical Partition (LPAR)
# on an IBM Power Systems managed system. LPARs are immutable: changing any
# managed attribute forces the partition to be destroyed and recreated.

##############################################
# Example 1: LPAR with dedicated processors
##############################################
resource "powerhmc_lpar" "dedicated" {
  system_name = "hmc-zz1"
  lpar_name   = "lpar-dedicated"
  # partition_type accepts "AIX/Linux" or "ibmi".
  partition_type = "AIX/Linux"

  # Memory configuration, in megabytes (MB).
  mem_config = {
    desired = 8192  # 8 GB
    min     = 4096  # 4 GB
    max     = 16384 # 16 GB
  }

  # Dedicated processor modes require desired/min/max_proc.
  proc_config = {
    proc_mode    = "share_idle_procs_active"
    desired_proc = 2
    min_proc     = 1
    max_proc     = 4
  }
}

##############################################
# Example 2: LPAR with shared (uncapped) processors
##############################################
resource "powerhmc_lpar" "shared" {
  system_name    = "hmc-zz1"
  lpar_name      = "lpar-shared"
  partition_type = "AIX/Linux"

  mem_config = {
    desired = 4096
    min     = 2048
    max     = 8192
  }

  # Shared processor modes (cap/uncap) require the virtual processor and
  # processing unit attributes. uncapped_weight (0-255) applies only to uncap.
  proc_config = {
    proc_mode            = "uncap"
    desired_virtual_proc = 2
    min_virtual_proc     = 1
    max_virtual_proc     = 4
    desired_proc_units   = "0.7"
    min_proc_units       = "0.1"
    max_proc_units       = "2.0"
    uncapped_weight      = 100
  }
}

##############################################
# Example 3: LPAR with virtual networks, storage, and fibre channel
##############################################
resource "powerhmc_lpar" "full" {
  system_name    = "hmc-zz1"
  lpar_name      = "lpar-app01"
  profile_name   = "default_profile"
  partition_type = "AIX/Linux"

  mem_config = {
    desired = 8192
    min     = 4096
    max     = 16384
  }

  proc_config = {
    proc_mode            = "uncap"
    desired_virtual_proc = 2
    min_virtual_proc     = 1
    max_virtual_proc     = 4
    desired_proc_units   = "0.5"
    min_proc_units       = "0.1"
    max_proc_units       = "2.0"
  }

  # Attach one or more physical I/O slots by location code. Short (e.g. "C7")
  # or full (e.g. "U78D3.001.WZS078A-P1-C7") location codes are accepted.
  io_slots = ["U78D3.001.WZS078A-P1-C7"]

  # Attach one or more virtual networks. slot_number (2-49) is optional;
  # the HMC auto-assigns a slot when it is omitted.
  virtual_networks = [
    {
      network_name = "app-vlan"
      slot_number  = 3
    }
  ]

  # Attach physical volumes served by one or more VIOS partitions.
  physical_volumes = [
    {
      vios_name        = "vios1"
      phy_volume_names = ["hdisk5", "hdisk6"]
    }
  ]

  # Attach virtual fibre channel adapters mapped to physical VIOS ports.
  # slot_number (2-49) is optional and auto-assigned when omitted.
  virtual_fibre_channels = [
    {
      vios_name = "vios1"
      port_name = "fcs0"
    }
  ]
  # Bound how long Terraform waits for the partition to be created or deleted.
  timeouts {
    create = "30m"
    delete = "20m"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `lpar_name` (String) The name of the LPAR partition.
- `mem_config` (Attributes) Memory configuration for the LPAR partition. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mem_config))
- `partition_type` (String) The partition type for the LPAR. Valid values are `AIX/Linux` and `ibmi`.
- `proc_config` (Attributes) Processor configuration for the LPAR partition. Required attributes depend on the processor mode (`proc_mode`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--proc_config))
- `system_name` (String) The name of the managed system where the LPAR will be created.

### Optional

- `io_slots` (List of String) List of physical I/O slot locations to assign to the LPAR partition.
- `physical_volumes` (Attributes Set) List of physical volumes to attach to the LPAR from VIOS servers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--physical_volumes))
- `profile_name` (String) The name of the partition profile. Must start with a letter or digit and contain up to 31 characters. Allowed symbols: `@#^/;:~,.-_=+{}`. Defaults to `default_profile`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `virtual_fibre_channels` (Attributes Set) Set of virtual fibre channel adapters to attach to the LPAR. Each adapter connects the LPAR to a physical fibre channel port on a VIOS server. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--virtual_fibre_channels))
- `virtual_networks` (Attributes Set) Set of virtual networks to attach to the LPAR. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--virtual_networks))

### Read-Only

- `lpar_uuid` (String) The unique identifier (UUID) of the LPAR partition.
- `reference_code` (String) The reference code associated with the LPAR partition.
- `rmc_state` (String) The current RMC (Resource Monitoring and Control) state of the LPAR partition.
- `state` (String) The current state of the LPAR partition.

<a id="nestedatt--mem_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mem_config`

Required:

- `desired` (Number) Desired memory allocation in megabytes (MB). Must be greater than 0 and a multiple of the memory region size for the managed system.
- `max` (Number) Maximum memory allocation in megabytes (MB). Must be greater than 0 and a multiple of the memory region size for the managed system.
- `min` (Number) Minimum memory allocation in megabytes (MB). Must be greater than 0 and a multiple of the memory region size for the managed system.

Read-Only:

- `current_mem` (Number) Current memory allocation in megabytes (MB).


<a id="nestedatt--proc_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `proc_config`

Required:

- `proc_mode` (String) Processor sharing mode. Valid values: `cap` (capped shared), `uncap` (uncapped shared), `keep_idle_procs` (dedicated keep idle), `share_idle_procs` (dedicated share idle), `share_idle_procs_active` (dedicated share idle active), `share_idle_procs_always` (dedicated share idle always).

Optional:

- `desired_proc` (Number) Desired number of dedicated processors. Required for dedicated processor modes.
- `desired_proc_units` (String) Desired processing units as a decimal string. Required for shared processor modes.
- `desired_virtual_proc` (Number) Desired number of virtual processors. Required for shared processor modes.
- `max_proc` (Number) Maximum number of dedicated processors. Required for dedicated processor modes.
- `max_proc_units` (String) Maximum processing units as a decimal string. Required for shared processor modes.
- `max_virtual_proc` (Number) Maximum number of virtual processors. Required for shared processor modes.
- `min_proc` (Number) Minimum number of dedicated processors. Required for dedicated processor modes.
- `min_proc_units` (String) Minimum processing units as a decimal string. Required for shared processor modes.
- `min_virtual_proc` (Number) Minimum number of virtual processors. Required for shared processor modes.
- `shared_proc_pool_id` (Number) The ID of the shared processor pool. Only applicable for shared processor modes.
- `uncapped_weight` (Number) The uncapped weight for the partition. Only applicable for uncapped shared processor mode. Valid range is 0-255. Defaults to 128 if not specified.

Read-Only:

- `current_proc` (Number) Current number of allocated dedicated processors.
- `current_proc_units` (String) Current processing units as a decimal string.
- `current_uncapped_weight` (Number) Current uncapped weight value allocated to the partition. Only applicable for uncapped shared processor mode.
- `current_virtual_proc` (Number) Current number of allocated virtual processors.


<a id="nestedatt--physical_volumes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `physical_volumes`

Required:

- `phy_volume_names` (Set of String) Set of physical volume names to attach from this VIOS to the LPAR.
- `vios_name` (String) The name of the VIOS server that owns the physical volumes.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.


<a id="nestedatt--virtual_fibre_channels"></a>
### Nested Schema for `virtual_fibre_channels`

Required:

- `port_name` (String) The name of the physical fibre channel port on the VIOS (e.g., 'fcs0', 'fcs2').
- `vios_name` (String) The name of the VIOS server that owns the physical fibre channel port.

Optional:

- `slot_number` (Number) The virtual slot number for the client fibre channel adapter on the LPAR. Valid range is 2-49. If not specified, the HMC will auto-assign a slot number within that range.


<a id="nestedatt--virtual_networks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `virtual_networks`

Required:

- `network_name` (String) The name of the virtual network to attach.

Optional:

- `slot_number` (Number) The virtual slot number for the client network adapter on the LPAR. Valid range is 2-49. If not specified, the HMC will auto-assign a slot number within that range.

Read-Only:

- `network_adapter` (Map of String) Map of network adapter location code to MAC address for this virtual network. Format: `{"location_code": "MAC_address"}`. MAC addresses are formatted with colons (e.g., `4A:79:55:27:8C:02`).

## Notes

<a id="choosing-a-processor-mode"></a>
### Choosing a processor mode

The valid attributes in `proc_config` depend on `proc_mode`. The provider
validates this at plan time:

* **Shared modes** — `cap`, `uncap`: the user can set `desired_virtual_proc`,
  `min_virtual_proc`, `max_virtual_proc`, `desired_proc_units`, `min_proc_units`,
  and `max_proc_units`. The dedicated attributes (`desired_proc`, `min_proc`,
  `max_proc`) must not be set. `uncapped_weight` (0-255) applies only to `uncap`.
* **Dedicated modes** — `keep_idle_procs`, `share_idle_procs`,
  `share_idle_procs_active`, `share_idle_procs_always`: the user can set `desired_proc`,
  `min_proc`, and `max_proc`. The shared attributes (virtual processors,
  processing units, `shared_proc_pool_id`, `uncapped_weight`) must not be set.

### Physical volumes and redundancy

In a dual-VIOS environment, specifying a physical volume on one VIOS is
sufficient. The provider identifies the same underlying disk on the peer VIOS
using its UDID/UUID and automatically attaches it from both sides — you do not
need to list the corresponding disk entry for the second VIOS explicitly.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# LPARs are imported using the managed system name and LPAR name,
# separated by a forward slash: <system_name>/<lpar_name>
terraform import powerhmc_lpar.dedicated hmc-zz1/lpar-dedicated
```
